negative_findings.description: No Mastercard or Visa press release naming a specific Kosovo bank partnership, contactless launch or tokenization deployment was located in this pass. Scheme newsrooms surfaced only global/EU-level announcements.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searched scheme newsrooms and general web; all hits were global tokenization/wallet stories with no Kosovo-specific item.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Card schemes are usually a reliable indirect discloser of issuer-side product launches; their absence for Kosovo means issuer/processor changes must be inferred from app metadata, BQK card statistics and local media instead.

negative_findings.description: No public evidence found linking a Kosovo bank to a named card-management / issuer-processing platform (BPC SmartVista, OpenWay Way4, Nexi/SIA, Euronet) or to a named ATM hardware supplier (Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos) for its Kosovo estate.
negative_findings.result_summary: Vendor-name searches returned only generic ATM-industry comparison articles; no Kosovo customer reference pages surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Card issuing/processing and ATM hardware are core procurement categories for this workstream; the gap means supplier identity here currently rests on hypotheses that need a different route (procurement records, ATM screen/branding observation, job ads, EMV certification lists).

negative_findings.description: No Serbian-language (sr) vendor or bank disclosure specific to Kosovo banking technology procurement was found. The sr-language pass returned only the Central Bank of Kosovo's own Serbian-language site pages (payment-system oversight, laws, retail payments strategy) — regulatory, not vendor, content.
negative_findings.result_summary: Serbian query on core banking implementation/contract/supplier returned bqk-kos.org ?lang=sr pages and Wikipedia only.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Serbian is a mandatory coverage language for Kosovo; the absence of sr vendor disclosure suggests supplier communication in this market runs in Albanian and English, and that sr coverage should be pursued via Serbian regional vendor/media outlets rather than Kosovo-hosted sr content.

negative_findings.description: No cybersecurity vendor was found publishing a named Kosovo bank as a customer reference. Kosovo-based security firms (Cyber Threat Defense, Cingerr, an unnamed Kosovo/Belgium boutique advertising via the Enterprise Europe Network) describe services but not banking clients.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches returned service-listing and directory pages; no bank logos, no case studies, no partnership announcements.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Bank security suppliers are normally kept confidential by design, so this category will likely never yield vendor-side disclosure; collection should pivot to BQK/regulatory IT-risk reporting, job advertisements and conference sponsorships.

negative_findings.description: A Printec Kosovo country contact page appeared in search results at a legacy-style URL (printecgroup.com/en/contact/27-contacts/6-kosovo.html) alongside the current site structure at printecgroup.com/offices-locations/. Not fetched, so its liveness is unknown and it may be a moved/legacy path.
negative_findings.result_summary: Two competing URL patterns for the same vendor's Kosovo presence; recorded as unverified rather than dead or live.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms a Kosovo office exists for at least one ATM/POS supplier, but the canonical Kosovo page must be resolved by the deterministic verification pass before being used as a monitored endpoint.

coverage_gaps.description: Card management systems, issuer/acquirer processing and the national card switch for Kosovo have no identified vendor-side source. Which platform processes Kosovo issuers, and whether processing is in-house, group-level (Raiffeisen/NLB/BKT/Ziraat parents) or outsourced regionally, is entirely unresolved.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pursue via non-PR routes: BQK payment-instrument oversight and licensing documents; parent-group annual reports (RBI, NLB, BKT, Ziraat, ProCredit Holding) which disclose group IT platforms serving Kosovo subsidiaries; EMV/scheme certification vendor lists; LinkedIn job ads at Kosovo banks naming a platform by name.

coverage_gaps.description: Serbian-language (sr) vendor disclosure coverage for Kosovo is effectively empty. Only BQK's own sr pages were reached; no sr vendor press release, case study or trade article about Kosovo banking technology was found.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated sr pass against Serbian and regional vendor/media domains (asseco.rs, Comtrade, Halcom sr, Biznis.rs, eKapija, Nova ekonomija) using sr terms: 'osnovni bankarski sistem', 'implementacija', 'ugovor', 'dobavljač', 'platni sistem', 'kartično poslovanje', 'referentni klijent'. Also cover the sr-language media serving northern Kosovo.

coverage_gaps.description: Several Kosovo banks have no vendor attribution at all in this pass — notably Banka Ekonomike, TEB SHA, PriBank (platform vendor, as distinct from IPKO as infrastructure partner) and ProCredit Bank Kosovo (whose app package was not resolved).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Complete a bank-by-bank technographic sweep: capture every Kosovo bank's Android package id and iOS bundle, e-banking login page vendor fingerprints (favicon, JS paths, copyright footers, TLS certificate SANs) and web-token/mToken app publishers. Package-prefix fingerprinting proved the single most productive technique in this cell.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor customer-logo walls and gated case-study libraries (ASEE, Temenos, Backbase, Printec, Montran) were not systematically enumerated; several sit behind forms or JavaScript rendering and were not fetched in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a rendering-capable fetch step for vendor 'customers'/'references'/'case studies' pages, plus sitemap.xml enumeration and Wayback Machine differencing to catch logos that were added and later removed — removals are themselves a churn signal.

coverage_gaps.description: Private-sector bank procurement in Kosovo produces no public tender record, so vendor selection at the eight commercial banks is invisible except when a party chooses to publicise it. Only BQK-side procurement is systematically disclosed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Treat local Albanian-language media PR items and app/web technical fingerprints as the primary substitutes; additionally monitor Kosovo business-registry filings (ARBK) for vendor subsidiary registrations and monitor bank annual reports' operational-risk and outsourcing sections, where material outsourcing arrangements are sometimes named.

brief: Kosovo's vendor-side disclosure landscape is thin on formal press releases and rich in technical fingerprints. The productive sources fall into four groups: (1) regional platform vendors whose Kosovo footprint is provable indirectly — Asseco/ASEE behind BPB, Ziraat Kosova and NLB Prishtina via hr.asseco.android.jimba.* app packages, New Frontier behind Raiffeisen Kosovo, Halcom's historic Raiffeisen mobile-bank launch — with app-store package and developer metadata the single highest-yield technique in this cell; (2) genuine vendor press releases at the national-infrastructure layer, above all Montran's CSD/RTGS implementation at the Central Bank of Kosovo; (3) Albanian-language local media carrying bank-supplier partnership PR that never reaches international vendor sites, exemplified by PriBank's selection of IPKO for critical banking infrastructure and cybersecurity; and (4) official BQK and e-Prokurimi contract-award notices, the only mandatory public record, which cover the central bank but not the eight commercial banks. The hard gaps are card management and issuer processing, ATM hardware supply, cybersecurity vendors, and Serbian-language coverage — none produced a single Kosovo customer reference in this pass.
